description_full: The North West Company Inc., through its subsidiaries, engages in the retail of food and everyday products and services in northern Canada, rural Alaska, the South Pacific, and the Caribbean. The company operates Northern stores, which offers food, general merchandise, and financial services that include cheque cashing, ATMs, and prepaid card products; NorthMart stores that provides fresh food, apparel, and health products and services; and Quickstop convenience stores that provides ready-to-eat food products, fuel, and related services. It also operates Giant Tiger junior discount stores, which offers family fashion, household products, and food products; Valu Lots discount center and direct-to-customer food distribution outlets for remote communities; solo market, a full service grocery; Pharmacy and Convenience stores; and NWC Motorsports, a dealership that offers sales, service, parts and accessories for Ski-doo, Honda, Can-am and other premier brands. In addition, the company also engages in distribution of produces and fresh meats; provides contract tele-pharmacist services; and engages in shipping services. Further, it operates Alaska Commercial Company stores that provides food and general merchandise to remote and rural regions; Pacific Alaska wholesale, a distributor to independent grocery stores, commercial accounts, and individual households; Riteway food markets; and Cost-U-Less mid-size warehouse stores. Additionally, the company also offers gasoline. The North West Company Inc. was formerly known as North West Company Fund and changed its name to The North West Company Inc. in January 2011. The North West Company Inc. was founded in 1668 and is headquartered in Winnipeg, Canada.

financial_summary: North West Company, Inc. (The) is a small-cap consumer defensive business with a $1.9B market cap on $1.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +1% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 15% against a 6% cost of capital, a 9-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 33%.

The business throws off $98M in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.00× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 11.8×.

Shareholder yield of 3.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

news_headlines.title: North West (OTCMKTS:NNWWF) Stock Falls 8.1% – Here’s Why

sect: Its 8% operating margin is roughly in line with the Consumer Defensive median (7%).
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.01x).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.07 across 172 companies in the universe; the top four hold 38% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 23% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 3% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 26% and a beta of 0.18, it is more defensive than the market.
Trading is thin (about $291K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.

val: The stock trades 32% below its DCF fair value of $59.63, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 23%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $46.05 to $80.01 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.

Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 5.1% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 6.3% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 0.5% annual cash-flow growth, 7pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 15% clears the cost of capital of 6.0% by 9pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.02).
It runs a 33% gross margin and converts 5% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 2.00x.
ROE of 17% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.0x equity multiplier).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 1.0x net debt to EBITDA ($63.3M of cash against $307.6M of debt), with interest covered 11.8x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 5.1, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 1.2% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 34% of profits supports about 5.1% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.1%), and institutions hold 39%.
It returns 3.4% a year to shareholders (0.5% in buybacks and 2.9% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 15 consecutive years.
people: With about 7,001 employees, each generates about $260K of revenue, 0.5x the Consumer Defensive median.
That works out to $14K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.4M (5x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
